harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built a 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster from scratch on node1-3 (bootstrapped on node1, joined node2/node3 via rsync SST), created an application database (appdb.orders) with sample data and an app user, then added node4 as a fourth member which received the existing data via SST and successfully accepted a write that replicated to all other nodes. Completed the mandatory sequential restart protocol on all four nodes, preserving quorum throughout, with each node's boot_id changing and each node rejoining the cluster as Synced with all data intact afterward.
actions_performed: Installed mariadb-server, mariadb-server-galera, and galera packages on all four RHEL10 nodes via dnf
Populated /etc/hosts with CLUSTER_HOSTS on all nodes
Opened firewalld ports 3306/tcp, 4567/tcp+udp, 4568/tcp, 4444/tcp on all four nodes (SELinux mysqld_port_t already covered these ports)
Edited /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on node1-3 to set wsrep_on=1, cluster name, cluster address gcomm://node1,node2,node3,node4, per-node wsrep_node_name/address, sst_method=rsync
Bootstrapped the cluster on node1 via galera_new_cluster, then started mariadb on node2 and node3, confirming each joined as Synced with cluster_size incrementing 1->2->3
Created appdb.orders table with 3 sample rows and an appuser account with a locally generated random password (not printed) on node1; confirmed replication to node2/node3
Configured galera.cnf on node4 identically and started mariadb, observing SST-based join reaching cluster_size=4 and Synced state with all prior application data present
Executed a write on node4 (INSERT) and confirmed it replicated back to node1, node2, and node3, proving node4 accepts writes like the other members
Enabled mariadb on boot on node1-3 (node4 auto-enabled via systemctl enable --now)
Captured baseline boot_id and cluster health (Synced, cluster_size=4, 4 rows) on all four nodes before restarts

Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 sequentially one at a time using systemctl reboot, polling each until exec access returned and confirming a changed boot_id, then verifying mariadb auto-started, rejoined as Synced with cluster_size=4, and appdb.orders row count intact

evidence.requirement: Initial 3-node Galera cluster formed and healthy (node1-3)
evidence.summary: node1 bootstrapped as Primary (size=1); node2 joined and Synced (size=2); node3 joined and Synced (size=3)

evidence.requirement: Application data exists and replicates across original 3 members
evidence.summary: appdb.orders created with 3 rows on node1; identical rows confirmed present on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: node4 added as fourth member and carries existing data
evidence.summary: node4 joined via SST reaching cluster_size=4/Synced and SELECT showed all 3 pre-existing rows present

evidence.requirement: node4 accepts writes like other members
evidence.summary: INSERT executed on node4 and the new row was confirmed replicated to node1, node2, and node3

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id 03408ac4->10e2db60 after systemctl reboot; post-restart mariadb active, cluster_size=4, Synced, 4 rows intact

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id 19062a82->56cfffd8 after systemctl reboot; post-restart mariadb active, cluster_size=4, Synced, 4 rows intact

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id b17495e3->4d6c8034 after systemctl reboot; post-restart mariadb active, cluster_size=4, Synced, 4 rows intact

evidence.requirement: node4 restart: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: boot_id d9f8550d->63a70cb8 after systemctl reboot; post-restart mariadb active, cluster_size=4, Synced, 4 rows intact

evidence.requirement: Final overall cluster health after all restarts
evidence.summary: node1 shows wsrep_cluster_status=Primary, cluster_size=4, all Synced, 4 rows in appdb.orders after full restart cycle
